raṭṭhapāla.notes: MN 82 tells of the son of Thullakoṭṭhika’s leading family who goes forth and later receives leftover porridge at his father’s house. The references landing in MN 11 and MN 81 miss that episode. The distinction for going forth out of faith is at AN 1.210.

revata.notes: AN 1.203 names Revata Khadiravaniya as foremost among forest dwellers. The next segment, AN 1.204, names Kaṅkhārevata as foremost in meditation. The packet supplies no entry for him or for the past Buddha. MN 118 gives Revata’s name alone. The cited admonition to Cālā, Upacālā and Sīsūpacālā is at Thag 1.42. Thag 1.43 belongs to Sumaṅgala. Thag 14.1 names the forest elder in the compound Khadiravaniyarevato.

reṇu.notes: Both DPD senses describe one king. DN 19:29.3 names Disampati’s son, 34.2 records his accession, and 36.2 gives him the central kingdom. The ensuing list of the seven Bhāratas includes him at 36.15–16.

rohitassa.notes: In AN 4.45 and SN 2.26 the godling recalls his life as the seer Rohitassa. AN 4.46 retells their conversation. The citations to AN 4.43–44 and SN 2.25 fall outside it. Both accounts describe the seer striding from the eastern ocean to the western one, reversing the entry’s direction. The people named in SN 15.20 have their own Rohitassā entry.

rohitassā.notes: SN 15.20:3.2–5 names the people, the mountain Vaṅkaka and the Buddha Koṇāgamana. The nominative Rohitassā at 3.4 also brings up the individual godling’s lemma. Rohitassāpare duve in the chapter index at AN 4.50:13.2 counts the two Rohitassa discourses about the godling.

roruka.notes: DN 19:36.6 explicitly pairs Roruka with the Sovīras. The following list includes King Bharata but does not explicitly pair each king with a city.

roruva.notes: The verse naming the hell is SN 1.39:4.3. The page reference also reaches SN 1.40, the younger Kokanadā’s verses.

rādha.notes: AN 1.233 names Rādha as the disciple who inspires eloquent teachings. DPPN glosses the distinction as speaking extemporarily. The questioner appears in SN 22.71 and SN 23.1. DPD’s SN 22.7 has no named questioner, and the page match at SN 22.159 has Ānanda. Thag 2.7 attributes the two rain-and-roof verses to Rādha.

rāhu.notes: The seizures of the moon and sun are in SN 2.9 and SN 2.10. SN 2.8 concerns Tāyana. Of the adjacent AN page matches, AN 4.15, AN 4.50 and AN 5.197 name Rāhu. DN 20:12.12 calls him Rāhubhadda in a joined form. Snp 3.4:17.2 uses the eclipse compound rāhuggahaṇā, and MN 13:14.3 names a punishment called ‘Rāhu’s mouth’. These compounds have their own dictionary lines.

rāhula.notes: The speaker calls himself both Rāhula and the Buddha’s son in Thag 4.8. Of the three AN ranges cited, the distinction for eagerness to train is at AN 1.209.

rājagaha.notes: DN 19:1.2 places the Buddha at Rājagaha. Its list of the seven cities laid out by Govinda at 36.3–10 does not include Rājagaha. The entry draws the city’s founding tradition from another source.

rājakārāma.notes: Nandaka visits the Royal Monastery in MN 146. SN 55.11:1.1 places the Buddha there in Sāvatthī. The adjacent SN 55.10 belongs to the Ñātika sequence.

sabbamitta.notes: DN 14:1.11.6 explicitly names Kassapa’s chief attendant. Thag 2.15 attributes its pair of verses to Sabbamitta Thera, and the chapter index at Thag 2.20:3.3 lists him after Somamitta. Sirimā speaks the verses preceding that index. At Thag 14.1:4.1 Revata describes himself as a friend and companion to all (sabbamitto sabbasakho). The tap there supplies only personal-name senses.

sabhiya.notes: Thag 4.3 attributes its verses to Sabhiya Thera, and Snp 3.6:54.2–3 records the wanderer Sabhiya’s ordination and arahantship. The only candidate describes Sabhiya Kaccāna, named in MN 127 and in SN 44.11, where Vacchagotta questions him at Ñātika. DPPN itself treats the identity with the other Sabhiya as conjectural. SN 44.10 has Vacchagotta questioning the Buddha.

saccaka.notes: MN 35 and MN 36 both name Saccaka Nigaṇṭhaputta and address him as Aggivessana. DPPN says he became a follower. MN 35:27–30 records his admission about the debate and his meal offering, with no declaration of refuge.

sahadhammā.notes: DN 20:15.5 lists the Sahadhammas alongside the Varuṇas. Sujato and DPPN take the name as plural. DPD flags a singular commentarial reading.

sahajāti.notes: AN 10.24 and AN 10.85 place Mahācunda at Sahajāti among the Cetis. AN 6.46:1.2 gives the location as sayaṁjātiyaṁ. SN 56.30:1.1 uses sahañcanike for the setting of Gavampati’s discourse. Sujato renders both as Sahajāti. SN 56.29 gives no such setting.

sahali.notes: SN 2.30:3.1 names the godling who speaks about Makkhali Gosāla. SN 2.29 concerns Susīma. DN 20:14.1 lists what Sujato renders as the Sahalī gods. That line gives no grounds for identifying the individual speaker.

sahampati.notes: Sahampati’s request that the Buddha teach is explicit in MN 26 and SN 6.1. DN 16:6.10.2 attributes the verse at the Buddha’s death to the compound brahmāsahampati, which has its own dictionary line. The parallel at SN 6.15 gives his name separately. AN 4.21 contains the exchange about revering the Dhamma. AN 4.9–10, SN 6.14, SN 11.15–16, SN 47.17 and SN 48.58 are citation matches without a named Sahampati.

sajjha.notes: AN 9.8 names Sajjha at Gijjhakūṭa. The wanderer in AN 9.7 is Sutavā. Both names recur in the chapter index at AN 9.10:2.3.
